recipes.name: Slow Cooker Beef Stew
ingredients_raw: 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed golden mushroom soup

steps.text: Place carrots, potatoes, mushrooms, onion, and celery in the slow cooker. Place stew meat over vegetables.
In a medium bowl, combine soup mix with can of soup. Add water and mix together well. Pour this in the slow cooker over meat and vegetables.
Add water as needed so that liquid comes just to the bottom of meat.
Cook on Low setting overnight, adding more water as necessary in the morning. Continue cooking all day to reach 24 hours total.

raw_recipe.headline: Slow Cooker Beef Stew
raw_recipe.description: In this slow cooker stew, carrots, potatoes, mushrooms, onions, and celery are cooked in dried onion soup mix and condensed golden mushroom soup.

review.reviewBody: I wasn't able to start this the night before, so I cooked it for 6 hours on high and it came out perfect! I used beef broth instead of the water, added a few more carrots and potatoes than the recipe called for, and I only added 1/2 an onion (and a small one at that), as I thought it might be a little too "oniony" with a whole onion AND the onion soup mix too. I also added some chopped parsley and a little bit of black pepper. The gravy was kind of thin, so an hour before it was done I added 2 tablespoons of cornstarch mixed with a little bit of the gravy, stirred it back into the pot and let it cook (on high) the last hour with the lid off. This thickened it up just beautifully! I served it with crusty rolls for sopping up all the gravy. I thought this was really good! When my husband took his first bite of the stew all he said was "Mmmmmmmmmm!", so I guess it was a winner with him too! :)

Followed the recipe with a few changes and it was so tasty. Omitted the mushrooms and added onion instead of soup mix. Lightly browned the stew meat and onions in olive oil, adding 2 tablespoons of flour and a half cup of water to make a little gravy. 

Added 1 can of stewed tomatoes, 1 can of corn, and 1 cup of greens beans 1 hour before end time. Also seasoned with lemon pepper and parsley.
Great recipe i added more seasonings along with some Worcestershire sauce. I thickened it at the last hour with flour. It didn't require to be started the night before. 8 hours on high was perfect.

Pretty good! would give it 4.5 stars if I could. I, too, was unable to start this the night before and honestly glad I didn't. Even on low I would think the veggies would be complete mush after all that time. I started mine on high at 10 am, turned it down to low after 4 hours and the meat was spoon tender by 7pm. With 1 hour to go I added 2 Tbs of corn starch to the stew and let it cook the last hour with the lid off and it thickened up PERFECTLY. I used vegetable broth instead of water and added about 2/3 cup of red wine (cab merlot blend) and 2 cloves of garlic to the mix. I was also a little heavy handed with the other veggies as I had stuff to use up. All in all this is a tasty recipe I will definitely make again although I think I may wait to put the veggies in at the half way point next time so they are not sooooooo soft.

This was a great starter for stew. It needed more flavor though. I had to thicken at the end. About an 45 minutes before serving I melted 4 TBLS of butter and slowly added 1/4 cup of flour. Once that was all mixed I slowly added juice from the stew until it was nice and creamy. I slowly added back to the stew. It gave it a great consistency, just like Mom used to make. Thanks for sharing.

This is so good and easy to make. I used 2 cans of soup and no onion soup mix. Doubled the vegetables and seasoned with garlic and parsley salt. Cooked on high for six hours then cooked 10 hours overnight. Turned out perfect def a do over

I loved this stew and my family enjoyed it as well. I did add about a heaping Tablespoon of cornstarch to thicken it also I added one large parsnip cut into small pieces. Frozen peas were added about a 1/2 hour before serving (about 1 cup) I cooked this in a lg. crock pot. It was delicious! I served it with homemade biscuits.

Took into account all the reviews and my rating is based on the following changes:

Used 1/2 an onion instead of a whole onion, added more carrots and celery. Added 1/2 cup of red wine. I browned the flour meat first, then poured the onion soup/broth/mushroom soup mixture over it. 

Cooked WITHOUT vegetables for 3 hours on low, then added vegetables in for the last 5 hours. The carrots came out just right - putting all the veggies in in the beginning will cause them to be soggy and overcooked.

Just before I put the veggies in, I tasted the gravy and it tasted bland. So I added a packet of slow cooker beef stew seasoning - this is what added the kick the stew was missing.

Was very skeptical at first but the stew came out beautifully. I also boiled the potatoes separately and threw them in cooked at the end, so they wouldn't absorb too much of the wine/spice flavoring.

This was so yum! I made a few alterations based on what others said. I used 3 cups of water, 1 can of beef broth, a pckge of Mccormick seasoning (instead of onion mix) and 1 can reg mush soup since I didn't have golden. I also added a couple dashes of worceshire sauce. The veggies I added were red potatos, peas, carrots, onion and celery. I made this the reg way last time and it was a little bland. Much better with the alterations!

Really good. Like others said, no need to cook overnight. Eight hours on low in the crock pot was just fine. The sauce was a little soupy, so I added some cornstarch to thicken. The family doesn't really like mushrooms, so more for me.

pretty good!! Used 1 can of beef broth instead of the water. I don't know why you need to cook this overnight, I put it on at 9am, added the carrots & potatoes about noon, added the onions, celery & garlic about 2 hours later. We were eating about 6pm. Served with some nice sour dough bread!

I made this for my hubby for supper tonight. It kept him begging for more. The kids loved it too. It really has a certain tangy taste that I can't quite describe nor explain. Definitely put us into a food coma. Good Night! 😴🤤💯👅

Excellent recipe. I think this is the best beef stew that I ever had. So flavorful and tender. I made no changes to the recipe. 

The only changes that I'm going to make next time is to add some extra potatoes and carrots, as I think some of the reviewers have done.

Not sure yet. First, I started it in the morning, but I don't have to have it ready for 11 hours, so I figured that would work. I didn't add carrots (to me it changes the flavor too much) or celery (I didn't have any), and I added green chile (a must where I live). I plan to add broccoli and cauliflower with four hours left. I'll let you know how changing out the vegetables works.
It was okay. If I make it again I will not add mushrooms and there was too much meat. Also would add more flavor.

Well, actually GETTING READY to make it! But may I just say the veges smell DELICIOUS! Will try to follow up with a better review, but I know it will be amazing from the ingredients and methods. :) Thanks for the recipe!
My husband doesn't like beef stew, but said this was the best stew he had ever had. High praise from him!
I did not use the golden mushroom soup, nor any mushrooms. I used 2 packets of Onion Soup mix, and maybe a teaspoon of Browning and Seasoning sauce.

I made a similar version of this just because I did not have all the ingredients it asked for. I used all the listed veggies but used more, used cream of mushroom soup, beef broth and water, 1 can tomatoes paste. I am on a restricted diet from potatoes so I just left them out. I have made this recipe exactly the way it is written also and love it. It's a great meal and easy to prepare in a crock pot. I did brown my meat first in flour with salt and pepper in a fry pan in olive oil. I like my stew more of a gravy and the flour helps with that.
